The supplied text had several garbled/cut-off fragments (mid-sentence corruption, likely a copy-paste glitch) -- repaired to complete sentences preserving the evident intended meaning; every repair is logged verbatim in FACTCHECK.md. metadata.description: A structured, checkpoint-by-checkpoint validation of the first real stage-v1.0.0 deployment: triggering the pipeline with a real release tag, triaging it stage by stage (auth, build, push, deploy) rather than as one black box, reading GitHub Actions' logs/step-summaries as the observability layer that makes that triage possible, and confirming the rollback path against that same deployed image before calling the pipeline verified end-to-end.
metadata.note: GitHub-dark skin for the four pipeline-mechanics beats (GitHubCallChain diagrams, matching the supplied slide structure), Claude-cream skin for the INTRO bookend, the outcome/closing cards, and the OUTRO. Narration text is the fellow-supplied script with garbled fragments repaired -- see FACTCHECK.md for the exact before/after of each repair.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW -- Claude cream skin, slide 1 title card
beats.narration_text: With staging fully configured, this week was about proving the pipeline by triggering a real deployment and methodically validating every stage of the process.

props.command: git tag stage-v1.0.0 && git push origin stage-v1.0.0
props.segment: End-to-End Validation — Triaging the First Staging Deployment
props.runningText: trigger → auth → build → push → deploy → rollback check…
output: validated checkpoint by checkpoint, not as one black box

beats.narration_text: The validation started by pushing a staging release tag, which triggered the full deploy pipeline — authentication, build, push, and deploy — exactly as it would for any real release.

nodes.d: a real release tag, not a test run

props.caption: Exactly the same pipeline any real release would run -- nothing special-cased for this validation.

beats.narration_text: Rather than treating a deployment as one big black box, I validated it checkpoint by checkpoint. First, authentication — confirming GitHub Actions successfully exchanged its identity for Google Cloud access. Next, the build stage — confirming the application compiled with the correct staging configuration baked in. Then the push stage — confirming the image landed correctly in Artifact Registry. And finally, the deploy stage — confirming Cloud Run picked up the new image and became healthy. Breaking the pipeline into these checkpoints makes it possible to pinpoint exactly where a run succeeds or needs attention, rather than guessing from a single pass or fail result.

nodes.d: GitHub Actions exchanged its identity for GCP access — pass
compiled with the correct staging config baked in — pass
image landed correctly in Artifact Registry — pass
Cloud Run picked up the new image and became healthy — pass

props.caption: Four checkpoints, four signals -- pinpoint where a run needs attention, don't guess from one pass/fail result.

beats.role_note: slide 4 -- GitHub Actions logs + step summaries
beats.narration_text: GitHub Actions provides detailed logs and step summaries for every run, which is what makes this kind of structured triage possible. Each step's output — the resolved environment, the image URI, the deployment result or status — becomes a checkpoint of its own. Reading that output and confirming correctness at each checkpoint is fast and precise, rather than guesswork.

nodes.d: full output per step, per job
resolved environment, image URI, deploy result

props.caption: Observability isn't a separate tool here -- it's the pipeline's own output, already there to read.

beats.role_note: slide 5 -- rollback validated against the same deploy
beats.narration_text: As part of this same validation pass, I also confirmed the rollback workflow against the newly deployed staging image — verifying that the same version could be re-deployed on demand, so the recovery path is proven at the same time as the forward deployment path.

nodes.d: alongside the forward path, not after it

props.caption: A forward deploy and a proven rollback, validated in the same pass -- not two separate weeks of trust.

beats.role_note: slide 6 -- the verdict card, Claude cream skin
beats.narration_text: By the end of this validation pass, the staging pipeline was completely validated from tag to live deployment — with a clear, repeatable process in place for diagnosing any stage of the pipeline going forward, not just for this release, but for every one after it.

artifactLines: Triggered with a real stage-v1.0.0 tag — the same pipeline every real release runs.
Validated checkpoint by checkpoint: auth, build, push, deploy — each with its own pass/fail signal.
Read, not guessed: GitHub Actions' own logs and step summaries confirmed each checkpoint.
Rollback proven in the same pass — the recovery path isn't a future unknown.
The result: tag to live deployment, fully validated, for this release and every one after it.

beats.role_note: slide 7 -- the closing line, Claude cream skin
beats.narration_text: The real outcome of this week wasn't just a successful deployment — it was a repeatable method for validating and triaging every deployment that follows.
